svg.title: Requests by our own agents on the evening of 8 November 2026 that broke a stated rule for automated readers, by when we classed them and what they were
svg.desc: Three blocks of small squares, one square per request our agents sent on the evening of 8 November 2026 that we judged to break a stated rule. The first and largest block, 113 squares, is the requests that broke a rule as we fixed it beforehand: 85 dark blue squares for requests to PyPI's interface for programs from one collector that read no robots.txt, all answered not found; 12 light blue squares for other requests that robots.txt rules ruled out, 5 of them because the file couldn't be reached; 11 orange squares for requests that came sooner than a Crawl-delay asked, 9 of them only because reading robots.txt counted as a request; and 5 grey squares for pages kept whole where the site asked for an excerpt. The second block, 59 hollow squares, is one reviewer's requests under a name that named no one, counted as breaches only after we saw them. The third, 19 dashed squares, is the requests that would also break the rule we adopted that evening, all in groups that name ClaudeBot. These are out of at least 3,497 requests found between 18:57 and 20:26 UTC; 90 of the 172 in the first two blocks were answered not found and 5 got no answer.
svg.text: Of 113 requests that broke a rule we fixed in advance, 85 came from one collector
Each square is one request by our own agents on the evening of 8 November 2026
that we judged to break a rule a site had stated.
Broke a rule as we fixed it
85 requests to PyPI's interface for programs, from one collector that read no robots.txt, all "not found"
12 other requests robots.txt rules ruled out, 5 because the file couldn't be reached
11 sooner than a Crawl-delay asked; 9 of them only because reading robots.txt counted as a request
5 pages kept whole where the site asked for no more than an excerpt
Out of at least 3,497 requests we found, sent 18:57 to 20:26 UTC. Of the 172 in the first two blocks,
90 were answered "not found" and 5 got no answer. 2 of the 113 were known before the count. Requests, not incidents or harm.
